text.p: Den Danske Bank share analysts on Thursday downgraded Danish construction, chemicals and packaging engineering group Superfos stock to a "match minus" from a "match plus" rating.

"We expect growth to continue at a low level in Sweden and central Europe, where Superfos derives a considerable amount of turnover and foresee no change in the current overcapacity in the Danish roadbuilding sector," the analysts said.
They also pointed to major new investments by Superfos in acquiring other firms as putting a strain on costs this year.
They said that the "match minus" rating meant that the Superfos share was expected to perform up to five percent worse than the market as a whole.
They estimated that Superfos' EPS (earnings per share) would be 49.1 this year and 53.3 next year compared with 1996's 45.2.

The Superfos share traded 10 crowns down at 780 at 1030 gmt. Superfos is involved in the current takeover battle for Danish roadbuilder Phoenix Contractors, but said it would not increase its last offer and Norway's Rieber & Son and Denmark's Icopal now head the field.
